goal: Produce a complete spec for adding helical (spiral) CT scanning to BasisSimulator.jl that integrates seamlessly with the existing volume scan, physics pipeline, workspace pattern, and GPU-native architecture. The spec must be detailed enough that AI agents can implement it without guessing.

context.current_state: Axial scanning works end-to-end: forward projection (Siddon), 16-step physics chain, FDK+iterative reconstruction, PCCT support. CTProtocol already has n_rotations field (unused). CTGeometry hardcodes Z=0 for all source/detector positions.
context.architecture: 5-part API: phantom → scanner → protocol → sim_opts → recon_opts. Zero-allocation workspace pattern. AcceleratedKernels.jl for GPU-agnostic execution.
context.key_constraint: Must integrate seamlessly — same API pattern, same physics pipeline, same workspace zero-alloc model. NOT a separate code path.

topics.title: Current Geometry and Projection Audit — Where Z=0 Is Hardcoded
topics.description: FIRST TOPIC. Read through every file that touches geometry, source/detector positions, or Z-coordinates. Map exactly where the circular-orbit assumption is baked in. Files to read: geometry/scanner.jl (CTGeometry constructor), projection/siddon.jl (ray tracing), reconstruction/fbp/fdk.jl (backprojection), api/workspace.jl (buffer allocation). For each Z=0 assumption: what changes for helical? Is it a parameter addition or a structural rewrite?

topics.title: Helical CT Geometry — Table Motion, Pitch, and Coordinate Transforms
topics.description: Research helical CT geometry. Define: pitch (table distance per rotation / beam collimation), table feed per angle, interpolation requirements. How does Z(θ) = z_start + pitch × collimation × θ/(2π) map into the existing CTGeometry struct? Can we extend CTGeometry with z_positions::Vector{Float64} per angle, or do we need a new struct? What pitch values are clinically relevant (0.5-1.5)? How does the n_rotations field in CTProtocol relate? Research how CatSim and TIGRE handle helical geometry.
sources: Buzug: Computed Tomography (textbook, Ch. 8 Spiral CT)

topics.title: Helical Forward Projection — Siddon with Table Motion
topics.description: The current Siddon ray tracer takes source and detector positions as inputs. For helical: the source/detector Z-positions change per angle. Research: Does the Siddon algorithm need modification, or just different input positions? What about the phantom — does it need to be larger in Z to cover the helical travel? How does the polychromatic accumulation change? Does the existing GPU kernel need changes or just different position buffers?

topics.title: Helical Reconstruction Algorithms — FDK-Helical vs Katsevich vs Rebinning
topics.description: The critical research topic. Current FDK assumes circular orbit. For helical there are multiple approaches: (A) Approximate FDK with helical weighting (Noo/Defrise/Clackdoyle 2003 weights, Tam-Danielsson window). (B) Exact Katsevich algorithm (2002, PI-line based). (C) Rebinning to parallel beam + 2D FBP (fastest but lowest quality). (D) ASSR (Advanced Single-Slice Rebinning). Research each: complexity, quality, which is standard in clinical scanners, which fits the existing workspace pattern. The recommendation should balance correctness with implementation effort.
sources: Katsevich 2002: Analysis of an exact inversion algorithm for spiral cone-beam CT
Noo, Defrise, Clackdoyle 2003: Single-slice rebinning with FDK weights
Turbell 2001: Cone-Beam Reconstruction Using Filtered Backprojection (PhD thesis)
Hsieh textbook Ch. 9 (Image Reconstruction: Helical CT)

topics.title: API Design — Seamless Helical in the 5-Part API
topics.description: Design the API changes. The user should be able to switch from axial to helical by changing ONE or TWO parameters, not by using a different code path. Research: What fields does CTProtocol need? (pitch, table_speed, n_rotations > 1). What does CTGeometry need? How does the workspace pattern adapt (larger sinogram buffers for multi-rotation)? How does simulate!() detect helical vs axial? What about PCCT + helical (dual complexity)?

topics.title: Physics Pipeline Compatibility — What Changes for Helical?
topics.description: Audit every step of the 16-step physics pipeline for helical compatibility. Most effects (noise, scatter, crosstalk, detector efficiency) should be angle-independent and work as-is. But: does the bowtie filter change with table position? Does scatter modeling change with helical geometry? Does BHC change? Does air scan calibration need adjustment? For each of the 16 steps: works as-is / needs minor modification / needs rewrite.

topics.title: Reference Implementations — TIGRE, CatSim, ASTRA, RTK
topics.description: Survey how existing CT simulation frameworks implement helical scanning. For each: (A) TIGRE (MATLAB/Python, GPU-accelerated). (B) CatSim/XCIST (our parity target). (C) ASTRA Toolbox (GPU cone-beam). (D) RTK (C++, ITK-based). What reconstruction algorithms do they use? How do they handle the geometry? What are their API patterns? Which is closest to our architecture? Code citations with file paths and line numbers.

topics.title: Validation and Testing — How Do We Know Helical Works?
topics.description: Define the test strategy. Ground truth options: (A) Compare against CatSim helical output. (B) Analytical phantoms with known helical solutions (Shepp-Logan spiral). (C) Compare helical FDK vs axial FDK on same phantom (should be similar for pitch ~1). (D) Measure artifacts: cone-beam artifacts should be REDUCED with helical. What metrics? HU accuracy, MTF, cone-beam artifact severity, z-resolution.

topics.title: SYNTHESIS: Helical CT Implementation Roadmap
topics.description: After all other topics complete: synthesize into a single coherent implementation plan with phased stories. Resolve the key decision: which reconstruction algorithm? Produce: API design spec, geometry changes, reconstruction algorithm pseudocode with GPU kernel design, physics pipeline compatibility matrix, test plan, story-level roadmap with dependencies.
